NDT training in Whiting: how it works for Whiting employers and technicians

Short answer: Atlantis NDT trains Whiting and Northwest Indiana technicians to ASNT SNT-TC-1A Level I, II and III in UT, PAUT, TOFD, RT, MT, PT, VT and ET. Theory runs live online or onsite at your facility in Lake County, the practical is done on real specimens under an ASNT Level III, and your employer certifies you under its written practice. There is no Atlantis classroom in Whiting; the course comes to your crew instead.

That model suits a town where one refinery and a ring of steel mills drive most of the inspection work. The technicians who most need a Level II upgrade are often the ones tied up in a turnaround at the refinery or an outage at a mill. Live online theory on Central time, followed by a practical block at your shop or a clean area on site, keeps people within reach of the work instead of sending them out of state for a two-week class. The sections below go further than the summary above: method by method, the certification steps, Indiana's brand-new radiation licensing arrangement, the real local training options, and the questions Whiting technicians and supervisors actually ask.

If you already know what you need, request a Whiting training quote. Cohort and onsite quotes come back within one business day.

SNT-TC-1A at a glance for Whiting crews

Here is the whole certification structure on one screen. Every Northwest Indiana employer that certifies to ASNT SNT-TC-1A works through the same building blocks; the hours and exam content come from that employer's written practice.

Building blockWhat it meansWho sets or signs it
Formal trainingClassroom hours in the method and levelYour written practice; recommended minimums are in the training requirements matrix
On-the-job experienceSupervised, logged time performing the methodLogged by the technician, verified by a certified supervisor
ExaminationsGeneral, specific and practicalAdministered and graded under a Level III
Vision testNear-vision acuity and colour contrast, at least annuallyRecorded in the certification file
CertificationWritten certification of the individualSigned by the employer under its written practice

ASNT Level I, II and III courses available in Whiting

Every course follows the ASNT SNT-TC-1A framework and is built to fit your written practice. Level I and II courses cover theory, equipment, technique and code acceptance criteria; Level III preparation covers the Basic and method exams. The table maps each method to the work Northwest Indiana employers actually do.

MethodLevelsWhat Whiting employers use it forPrerequisite
UT (thickness and shear wave)I, II, III prepCorrosion monitoring on refinery piping and vessels, weld inspection, thickness surveys on mill structures and tanksNone for Level I; Level I time and hours for Level II under your written practice
PAUT (phased array UT)II, III prepEncoded weld inspection during turnarounds, corrosion mapping on vessels and large-bore linesUT Level II or equivalent UT background
TOFD (time-of-flight diffraction)IIFlaw sizing in thick-wall pressure equipment welds, often alongside PAUTUT Level II
RT (radiographic testing)I, II, III prepWeld radiography on piping fabrication and repairs, film and digital interpretationRadiation safety training plus a recognised radiographer certification before working as a radiographer (see licensing below)
MT (magnetic particle)I, II, III prepCracks in carbon-steel welds, crane hooks, ladle and crane components, structural steel and rotating equipment in the millsNone for Level I
PT (liquid penetrant)I, II, III prepSurface defects on stainless and alloy piping, valves and non-magnetic partsNone for Level I
VT (visual testing)I, II, III prepWeld and fit-up inspection, external corrosion, structural condition surveysNone for Level I
ET (eddy current)I, II, III prepHeat exchanger and condenser tubing in the refinery and power plants, surface-crack work on non-ferrous partsNone for Level I

We point you to the SNT-TC-1A training requirements matrix for classroom and experience hours rather than quoting numbers here, because your written practice can require more than the recommended minimums and the auditor checks your document. Method detail sits on the UT Level 2 course, magnetic particle training and phased array training pages.

Method spotlight: UT and MT for a refinery-and-steel town

Whiting's inspection market has two personalities, and the methods follow them. On the refinery side, the work is pressure equipment: thickness readings at corrosion monitoring locations, weld inspection on piping repairs and new tie-ins, and PAUT or TOFD on thick welds where radiography would mean clearing a busy turnaround area. The BP Whiting Refinery processes a large share of heavy crude after its modernisation project a little over a decade ago, and heavier, higher-sulfur crude slates generally put more weight on corrosion monitoring and well-kept thickness data. A UT Level II who can produce repeatable readings and report them cleanly is valuable here.

On the steel side, the work is structural and mechanical. Integrated steel mills run overhead cranes, ladles, rolling equipment and heavy structures under constant load and heat. Magnetic particle testing on crane hooks, lifting gear and welded structures, UT on shafts, rolls and heavy plate, and visual inspection of structural steel are routine maintenance tasks. MT is one of the fastest methods to train for and one of the most used in the mills, which makes MT Level II a practical first certification for people moving into inspection from maintenance or welding.

Our practicals use real specimens that match this mix: piping welds with known flaws, corroded plate and step wedges for thickness work, and cracked forgings and welds for MT. For an employer cohort we can build the practical around parts from your own shop.

SNT-TC-1A certification path in Whiting, step by step

SNT-TC-1A is a recommended practice, so certification belongs to your employer, not to a school. The route a Whiting technician follows:

  1. Your employer's written practice. It documents how the company trains, examines and certifies NDT personnel. If you do not have one, a Level III writes it (see written practice development).
  2. Formal classroom training, live online or onsite in Lake County, for the hours your written practice requires.
  3. On-the-job experience, logged, signed and dated. Refinery owners and mill quality departments check these logs.
  4. General examination on method theory.
  5. Specific examination on your employer's procedures, equipment and codes.
  6. Practical examination on real specimens, administered and graded by a Level III.
  7. Vision test, repeated at least annually.
  8. Certification in writing by your employer, with recertification at the interval your written practice sets.

The recommended hours are in the training requirements matrix. For the full employer programme, see SNT-TC-1A training and certification.

Radiography licensing and site access in Whiting

This is the part of the Whiting picture that changed most recently. Indiana signed an agreement with the US Nuclear Regulatory Commission on 24 September 2026 and became the 41st Agreement State, with the agreement taking effect on 30 September 2026. From that date the Indiana Department of Homeland Security's Radioactive Materials Control Program, rather than the NRC, licenses and inspects most radioactive-materials users in the state, including industrial users. Indiana says it will honour NRC-issued licences that were in place when the agreement took effect. Radiography companies working in Whiting should still confirm with IDHS how their licence, renewals and inspections are handled now.

X-ray equipment was already state business before the agreement. Indiana requires radiation machine facilities, including industrial X-ray users, to register with the Indiana Department of Health under the radiological health rules in 410 IAC 5, which include a section on non-medical radiography. Radiographers themselves need a recognised radiographer certification, typically ASNT's Industrial Radiography Radiation Safety Personnel (IRRSP) certification or an Agreement State card. An SNT-TC-1A RT Level II certification is not the same thing; most radiographers need both. Our NDT radiation safety guide covers the general requirements.

Whiting crews often cross the state line. Refineries, chemical plants and mills on the Illinois side of the Chicago area are regulated by Illinois's own radiation programme, so a crew working on both sides needs reciprocity arrangements for each jurisdiction before taking a source across the border. Your radiation safety officer handles this; trainees just need to know it exists.

Site access is the other gate. Facilities with waterfront operations on Lake Michigan, the Indiana Harbor Ship Canal or the port at Burns Harbor may fall under the Maritime Transportation Security Act, in which case a TSA TWIC card is needed for unescorted access to secure areas. Not every assignment needs one, so ask the site. Refineries and mills also run their own contractor safety orientations, drug testing and permit-to-work training.

Where NDT technicians work in Whiting

Whiting is a small city with an outsized industrial footprint. The main sources of inspection work within a short drive are:

  • BP Whiting Refinery, the largest refinery in the Midwest and BP's largest anywhere, with fixed-equipment inspection programmes and periodic turnarounds that bring in large contractor crews.
  • Cleveland-Cliffs Indiana Harbor in East Chicago and U.S. Steel Gary Works, two large integrated steel complexes, plus Cleveland-Cliffs Burns Harbor further east along the lake.
  • Pipelines and tank terminals that move crude and products into and out of the region, including large crude terminals in Lake County.
  • Power generation and utilities serving Northwest Indiana, including the utility's generating stations and industrial cogeneration.
  • Fabrication and steel service shops in Hammond, East Chicago, Gary and the surrounding towns, supplying the refinery and the mills.
  • Bridges and highway structures on the Indiana Toll Road, the Borman Expressway and the Chicago Skyway approaches, plus rail infrastructure across the region.

The codes you will meet are the standard refinery and structural set: ASME Section V for NDT methods, ASME Section VIII and B31.3 for vessels and process piping, API 1104 for pipeline welding, AWS D1.1 for structural steel and AWS D1.5 for bridges. In-service refinery inspection references API 510, 570 and 653. We teach the NDT methods those codes require; API inspector authorisations and CWI are separate schemes that Atlantis does not train for, though many local employers ask for them alongside NDT certification.

For industry-specific content, see oil and gas NDT training and manufacturing NDT training.

If you are an individual without an employer, a classroom programme with a lab may suit you best. If you run a crew in Lake County, bringing the course to your facility usually costs less in lost shifts than sending people away.

Online, live-virtual or onsite NDT training for Whiting crews

  • Live online theory. Instructor-led sessions on Central time, with recorded material and quizzes between sessions. See NDT training online.
  • Live-virtual cohorts for your company. A private online class for your crew only, scheduled around shift rotations and outage windows.
  • Onsite at your facility. A Level III comes to your shop, refinery contractor yard or mill, teaches the practical block on your equipment and specimens, and administers exams under your written practice.

The practical portion cannot be done remotely under any credible written practice; it needs real equipment, real specimens and a Level III. Online delivery removes the travel and lost shifts from the theory. We schedule around refinery turnaround seasons and mill outages where we can, and split courses into blocks so people are not off the job for long. For multi-site programmes see corporate NDT training.

Ask about onsite training for your Whiting crew and tell us methods, levels, headcount and timing.

Level III services and written practices for Whiting NDT companies

Training only counts if it lands in a sound certification system. Many smaller inspection and fabrication companies in Northwest Indiana rely on an outside Level III, and refinery and mill owners audit contractor certification files. Atlantis provides:

  • Written practice development and review to SNT-TC-1A. See written practice development, written practices for refining contractors and written practices for steel and metals.
  • Level III of record and exam administration. See ASNT Level III consulting services.
  • Procedure writing and audit preparation. See Level III audit support for steel and metals and for refining.

An auditor will typically ask for the written practice, training records, experience logs, exam records with scores, vision tests and signed certifications. We set those files up so they answer the questions on first look. Book a Level III consultation before your next audit.

Practise before the practical exam

Our Practical NDT simulator lets trainees practise 12 methods in 5 environments: an NDT lab, a welding workshop, an aircraft hangar, an oil and gas site and a storage tank. The oil and gas site, storage tank and welding workshop are the closest match to work around Whiting. Use it to rehearse set-ups, scan patterns and reporting before you face a Level III.

It is practice only. It does not replace hands-on training on real equipment or the practical exam on real specimens.

Your instructor

Atlantis training is led by Anoop Rayavarapu, ASNT NDT Level III and founder of Atlantis NDT. He oversees course content, practical examinations and the written-practice work behind each certification, and leads ASNT Level III exam preparation directly.

Frequently asked questions about NDT training in Whiting

How do I get NDT certified in Whiting?

Under ASNT SNT-TC-1A your employer certifies you. You complete classroom training, log supervised experience, pass general, specific and practical exams under a Level III and a vision test, and the employer signs your certification under its written practice. Atlantis delivers the training and exams.

Is there an NDT school in Whiting or Northwest Indiana?

There is no dedicated NDT school in Whiting. The nearest classroom NDT certificate we know of is at Moraine Valley Community College in Palos Hills, Illinois. Ivy Tech's Lake County campuses run welding and industrial programmes. Atlantis has no Whiting classroom; we teach live online or onsite at your facility.

Can I take NDT training online in Indiana?

Yes, for the theory. Live online classes cover classroom hours; the practical training and exam are done in person on real specimens at your employer's site or an arranged location.

How long does UT Level 2 training take?

It depends on your written practice. SNT-TC-1A recommends minimum classroom and experience hours, and employers can require more; experience time is usually the longest part. See the training requirements matrix.

Do I need a licence for radiography in Indiana?

Your employer needs a radioactive-materials licence (now issued by IDHS since Indiana became an Agreement State on 30 September 2026) or an X-ray registration with the Indiana Department of Health, and you need a recognised radiographer certification such as ASNT IRRSP. Confirm current requirements with the state.

Does Indiana becoming an Agreement State change my training?

Not your SNT-TC-1A training. It changes which agency licenses and inspects your employer's radioactive-materials use. Radiation safety content stays based on the same federal-compatible rules.

Do I need a TWIC card to work in Whiting?

Only for unescorted access to the secure areas of MTSA-regulated waterfront facilities. Ask the site; many assignments do not need one.

What does NDT training cost in Whiting?

We quote on request because the price depends on method, level, group size, and whether the practical is onsite. Quotes come back within one business day. Request a Whiting training quote.

Can I use the GI Bill or WIOA for NDT training?

Those programmes pay only approved providers: the GI Bill needs a VA-approved programme, and WIOA uses Indiana's Eligible Training Provider List. Atlantis does not claim either approval, so check the VA's WEAMS search and the Indiana ETPL. The common route here is employer-paid training under the company's written practice.

Is ASNT certification recognised by Whiting employers?

SNT-TC-1A-based employer certification is the normal standard for NDT personnel at refineries, mills and inspection contractors in the region. Some roles also want API inspector authorisations or CWI, which are separate schemes.

Can you train our crew at our plant or mill?

Yes. A Level III comes onsite for the practical block and exams, with theory online beforehand, scheduled around turnarounds and outages.

Can I prepare for ASNT Level III with Atlantis?

Yes. We run preparation for the Basic and method exams. See ASNT Level III training and UT Level 2 practice questions.
